what_it_does: This paper solves a fundamental challenge in analog circuits: building a clock oscillator from resistors and capacitors that stays accurate across temperature and manufacturing variations. Open-loop designs drift too much; closed-loop designs (with feedback) are accurate but bloated with extra circuitry. This work uses an elegant compensation technique—replicate a reference resistor-capacitor network inside the oscillator feedback path, then cancel out the drift by subtracting out the path delay and voltage-offset errors that cause frequency wobble. The result: a tiny oscillator that consumes just 0.4 microwatts per megahertz clock speed and stays accurate to within ±9.83 parts-per-million across -40 to 125 Celsius, without needing tunable resistors or polynomial math for calibration.
